CDISC Submission Value: ABDUCTOR DIGITI MINIMI MUSCLE OF THE HAND
CDISC Definition: A muscle of the hand, in general extending from the pisiform bone, the pisohamate ligament, and the flexor retinaculum to the ulnopalmar margin of the proximal phalanx. Primary function is abduction of the little finger and flexion of the phalanx nearest the hand.
NCI Preferred Term: Abductor Digiti Minimi Muscle of the Hand

CDISC Synonym(s): Abductor Digiti Minimi; Abductor Minimi Digiti
CDISC Definition: A muscle in the foot, in general extending from the medial and lateral processes of the posterior calcaneal tuberosity to the lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the fifth toe and the fifth metatarsal; primary function is to abduct the fifth toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint and support the lateral arch.

A muscle in the foot, in general extending from the medial process of the posterior calcaneal tuberosity to the medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the big toe; primary function is to abduct and flex the big toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint.

A muscle of the hand, in general extending from the flexor retinaculum and the tubercles of the scaphoid and trapezium bones to the outer side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb. Primary function is abduction of the thumb away from the palm.
A skeletal muscle of the forearm originating from the posterior surfaces of the ulna and radius and the interosseous membrane. (NCI)
An additional renal vessel originating from the aorta and entering the kidney at the proximal or distal end of the organ. Accessory renal arteries are found in 26-30% of humans.
Two cup shaped areas, one each on the lateral side of the lower pelvis that house the head of the femur to form the ball and socket joint of the hip. (NCI)
The tendon that, in general, attaches the gastrocnemius muscle to the calcaneous bone in the tarsus.
The junction of the upper distal end of the scapula to the distal edge of the collarbone, also known as the acromion and the clavicle. (NCI)
The upper distal process of the scapula. (NCI)
The arteries that arise at the junction of the proximal and mid-right coronary artery conduit segments.

A muscle in the leg, in general extending from the external surface of the body of pubis and the anterior surface of the inferior pubic ramus to the pectineal line and the medial lip of the linea aspera; primary function is to adduct, flex, and rotate the thigh.

The larger of two heads of the adductor hallucis muscle, in general originating from the sheath of the peroneus longus tendon and the plantar surface of the bases of the second to fourth metatarsal bones in the foot.
NCI Preferred Term: Oblique Head of Adductor Hallucis Muscle

CDISC Definition: The smaller of two heads of the adductor hallucis muscle, in general originating from the deep transverse metatarsal ligament and the plantar surface of the metatarsophalangeal joints of the lateral three toes.
NCI Preferred Term: Transverse Head of Adductor Hallucis Muscle

CDISC Definition: A muscle in the thigh, in general extending from the external surface of the body of pubis to the middle third of the linea aspera; primary function is to adduct and medially rotate the thigh.

A muscle in the thigh, in general extending from the ischiopubic ramus and ischial tuberosity to the gluteal tuberosity of the femur, medial lip of the linea aspera, medial supracondylar ridge, and adductor tubercle; primary function is to adduct, flex, extend, and medially rotate the thigh at the hip joint.

A muscle of the hand that extends from the capitate and bases of the second and third metacarpals for the oblique head, and the anterior surface of body of the third metacarpal for the transverse head, to the base of proximal phalanx and extensor hood of the thumb; primary function is to draw the first metacarpal laterally to oppose the thumb toward the center of palm and rotate it medially.
The endocrine glands adjacent to the kidneys that consist of the outer adrenal cortex and the inner adrenal medulla in mammals.

CDISC Definition: The bony process of the sphenoid bone, extending from the side of the body of the sphenoid and curving upward, laterally, and backward.
The thickened bony structures in the mandible and maxilla that contain the sockets of the teeth.
Any of the terminal sacs in the lungs through which gas exchange takes place with the pulmonary capillary blood.
The fluid within the amniotic cavity which surrounds and protects the developing embryo. (NCI)
The junction of the common bile and main pancreatic ducts, which protrudes into the medial aspect of the descending duodenum at the major duodenal papilla.
A group of nuclei adjacent to the lateral ventricle of the brain within the temporal lobe, and is part of the limbic system.
The terminal section of the alimentary canal, which extends from the anorectal junction and ends at the anal opening. (NCI)
The area that includes the anus and the perianal skin.

The transitional zone between the moist, hairless, modified skin of the anal canal and the perianal skin.

One of the arteries of the thorax; in general it arises from the brachiocephalic artery or the aortic arch and branches into several arteries to supply blood to the head, neck, and arm/forelimb.
The vein that drains the axillary vein and joins the internal jugular vein to form the brachiocephalic vein. It runs parallel to the subclavian artery.
Adipose and connective tissue located deep to the dermis.
The potential body space between the arachnoid membrane and the dura mater.
The area of the larynx below the vocal cords down to the trachea. (NCI)
A body region relating to the area under or adjacent to the tongue.
The salivary gland located adjacent to the mandible.
Lymph node(s) adjacent to the mandible.
The area of the body that is located between the body of the mandible and the hyoid bone; it is formed by the submental and submandibular triangles.
The lymph nodes located between the anterior bellies of the digastric muscles. (NCI)

The area of the body that is located under the chin; it is bordered superiorly by the mylohyoid muscle, inferiorly by the platysma muscle, laterally by the anterior bellies of the digastric muscles, anteriorly by the mandible, and posteriorly by the hyoid bone.
The space between the neurosensory retina and retinal pigmented epithelial layer.
A muscle in the shoulder, in general extending from the subscapular fossa to the lesser tubercle of the humerus; primary function is to medially rotate the humerus.
One of the four rotator cuff muscle tendons in the shoulder; it is located on the anterior surface of the lesser tuberosity of the humerus and inserts into the lesser tuberosity of the humerus.
The portion of the midbrain composed of two parts, the pars compacta and pars reticulata.
The plane synovial joint between the talus and calcaneus bones of the foot.
The small coiled tubular glands in the skin that produce and secrete sweat.
The portion of the femoral artery distal to the branching of the deep femoral artery that runs close to the skin.
A lymph node located in a superficial part of the body.
Any of the veins that drain the subcutaneous tissue layers.
A ridge on the frontal lobe of the brain located above the superior frontal sulcus.

CDISC Submission Value: SUPERIOR MEDIASTINAL LYMPH NODE LEVEL VII
CDISC Definition: Lymph nodes in this group include pretracheal, paratracheal, and esophageal groove lymph nodes, extending from the level of the suprasternal notch cephalad and up to the innominate artery caudad. These nodes are at greatest risk of involvement by thyroid cancer and cancer of the esophagus. (AJCC 8th ed.)
NCI Preferred Term: Superior Mediastinal Lymph Node Group (Level VII)

CDISC Definition: The portion of the pubic ramus that lies between the body of the ilium and the inferior pubic ramus.

An intracranial venous sinus that lies in a superior and midline location above the interhemispheric fissure along the superior border of the falx cerebri of the brain. The sinus receives blood from the cerebral veins and drains posteriorly into the lateral sinuses of the brain, which in turn drain into the internal jugular veins.
A ridge on the outer surface of the temporal lobe between the horizontal portion of the fissure of Sylvius and the superior temporal sulcus. (NCI)

CDISC Synonym(s): Anterior Vena Cava; Cranial Vena Cava
CDISC Definition: The large vein that terminates in the right atrium and transports deoxygenated blood from the head, neck, arms, and chest to the heart.

A muscle of the forearm, in general extending from the posterior proximal shaft of the ulna and the lateral epicondyle of the humerus to the proximal third of the radius on the anterolateral and posterior surface; primary function is to supinate the forearm.

A depression found at the base of the neck that is bounded thusly: superiorly by the posterior belly of the omohyoid muscle; inferiorly by the clavicle; and medially by the sternocleidomastoid muscle.
A lymph node which is located above the clavicle. (NCI)
The upper part of the larynx, including the epiglottis; the area above the vocal cords.
A ridge on the anterior part of the inferior parietal lobe of the brain.
The superior portion of the occipital bone on the dorsal side of the foramen magnum; it is present during fetal development and later fuses with the occipital bone.
The lowest central region of the abdomen, below the umbilical region and between the two iliac regions. (NCI)
The portion of the abdominal aorta cranial to the renal arteries.

One of four muscles surrounding the glenohumeral joint, in general extending from the supraspinous fossa of the scapula to the greater tubercle of the humerus; primary function is to abduct the arm and provide muscular support to the shoulder.
One of the four rotator cuff muscle tendons in the shoulder; it lies in the subacromial space and inserts into the greater tuberosity of the humerus.
The part of the brain above the tentorium cerebellum. (NCI)
A minor branch of the sciatic nerve that includes the lateral and caudal sural nerves, which innervates the skin of the crus, tarsus and metatarsus.
Rigid, fibrous joints between the ossified bones of the skull.

A mass containing the cell bodies of sympathetic nerves. Sympathetic ganglia exist as paravertebral ganglia (located bilaterally adjacent to the spinal cord) or prevertebral ganglia (located close to the target organ).
The fluid within a joint capsule.
The connective tissue and synoviocytes that line the inner surface of the joint capsule.
The area of the skin innervated by the first thoracic spinal nerve, covering the medial aspect of the upper arm near the axilla (armpit).
The first thoracic vertebra counting from the top down. (NCI)
The area of the skin innervated by the tenth thoracic spinal nerve, corresponding approximately to the level of the umbilicus (navel).
The tenth thoracic vertebra counting from the top down. (NCI)

The area of the skin innervated by the eleventh thoracic spinal nerve, covering a horizontal segment of the lower abdomen, situated just below the T10 dermatome (which is at the level of the umbilicus), and extends around the body towards the back.
The eleventh thoracic vertebra counting from the top down. (NCI)
The area of the skin innervated by the twelfth thoracic spinal nerve, covering the lower abdomen and upper aspect of the groin area.
The twelfth thoracic vertebra counting from the top down. (NCI)
The area of the skin innervated by the second thoracic spinal nerve, covering the upper chest and extending to the upper medial aspect of the arm.
The second thoracic vertebra counting from the top down. (NCI)
The area of the skin innervated by the third thoracic spinal nerve, covering the upper part of the chest, just below the clavicle, and extending around the upper portion of the back.
The third thoracic vertebra counting from the top down. (NCI)
The area of the skin innervated by the fourth thoracic spinal nerve, located at the level of the nipples, extending around the chest and upper back.
The fourth thoracic vertebra counting from the top down. (NCI)
The area of the skin innervated by the fifth thoracic spinal nerve, located just below the T4 dermatome, and covers a horizontal band between the nipple line and the lower sternum.
The fifth thoracic vertebra counting from the top down. (NCI)
The area of the skin innervated by the sixth thoracic spinal nerve, located at the level of the xiphoid process of the sternum, wrapping around the mid-to-lower chest and back.
The sixth thoracic vertebra counting from the top down. (NCI)
The area of the skin innervated by the seventh thoracic spinal nerve and covers a horizontal band just below the T6 dermatome, extending around the lower part of the chest and the upper abdomen.
The seventh thoracic vertebra counting from the top down. (NCI)

The area of the skin innervated by the eighth thoracic spinal nerve, located below the T7 dermatome, wrapping around midway between the xiphoid process and the umbilicus, covering part of the upper abdomen.
The eighth thoracic vertebra counting from the top down. (NCI)
The area of the skin innervated by the ninth thoracic spinal nerve, covering a horizontal segment just above the umbilicus, extending around the middle section of the abdomen and back.
The ninth thoracic vertebra counting from the top down. (NCI)
A flexible appendage caudal to the sacrum.
The bone of the foot that connects with the tibia and fibula to form the ankle joint. (NCI)
A joint formed by the union of tarsal bones.
Any of the short bones between the tibiotarsal joint and the tarsometatarsal joint.
The dorsal part or roof plate of the midbrain, which consists of the pretectal area and the paired superior and inferior colliculi.
The flat area on either side of the head that is located posterior to the eye and forehead, anterior to the ear, and superior to the cheekbone.
A terminal branch of the external carotid artery that branches into the anterior and posterior temporal arteries. (NCI)

A large irregular bone situated at the base and side of the skull, connected with the mandible via the temporomandibular joint. The temporal bone consists of the squamous, tympanic and petrous parts. The petrous portion of the temporal bone contains the vestibulocochlear organ of the inner ear. (NCI)
The outermost layer of the temporal lobe of the brain, made up of gray matter.

The second largest of the four cerebral lobes, the temporal lobe is approximately twenty two percent of the total neocortical volume. The temporal lobe can be divided into two main sections: first, the neocortex, comprising its lateral and inferolateral surfaces, and its standard cerebral cortex; and, second, the mesial temporal lobe, which is sometimes referred to as the limbic lobe, and includes the hippocampus, the amygdala, and the parahippocampal gyrus. Grossly, the lobe extends superiorly to the Sylvian fissure, and posteriorly to an imaginary line, the lateral parietotemporal line, which separates the temporal lobe from the inferior parietal lobule superiorly and the occipital lobe inferiorly. The middle cranial fossa forms its anterior and inferior boundaries.
The joint between the head of the lower mandible and the temporal bone. (NCI)
A band of fibrous connective tissue that joins bone to muscle. (NCI)

CDISC Synonym(s): Tensor Fasciae Latae Muscle; TFL Muscle
CDISC Definition: A muscle of the gluteal region, in general extending from the iliac crest to the iliotibial tract of the fascia lata; primary function is to stabilize the knee in extension and in hip flexion.
A laminar extension of the dura mater that lies between, and separates, the cerebrum and the cerebellum. (NCI)
One of the four rotator cuff muscle tendons in the shoulder; it is located inferior to the infraspinatus tendon, deep to the deltoid muscle, and inserts into the greater tuberosity of the humerus.
The male gonad.
The portion of the diencephalon forming most of each lateral wall of the third ventricle.
A part of the lower limb, located between hip and knee. (NCI)

CDISC Synonym(s): 3RD DIAG; THIRD DIAGONAL BRANCH ARTERY SEGMENT
CDISC Definition: The third artery arising from the left anterior descending (LAD) artery that supplies the anterolateral wall, when counted from proximal to distal.

CDISC Synonym(s): 3RD OM; THIRD OBTUSE MARGINAL BRANCH ARTERY SEGMENT
CDISC Definition: The third artery arising from the left circumflex artery that supplies the lateral wall, when counted from proximal to distal.

CDISC Synonym(s): 3RD LPL; THIRD POSTEROLATERAL DESCENDING ARTERY SEGMENT
CDISC Definition: In an individual with a left-dominant heart, this is the third branch that arises from the circumflex artery atrioventricular groove continuation when counted from proximal to distal. It supplies the posterolateral wall.

CDISC Synonym(s): 3RD RPL; THIRD RIGHT POSTEROLATERAL ARTERY SEGMENT
CDISC Definition: In an individual with a right-dominant heart, this is the third branch that arises from the right coronary artery distal to the right posterior descending artery, when counted from proximal to distal.
The section of the aorta between the lower border of the fourth dorsal vertebrae and the aortic opening in the diaphragm. (NCI)
An artery that branches from the axillary artery or one of its branches, and that supplies the muscles and organs of the thorax.
The cavity enclosed by the ribs between the diaphragm and the neck.
Lymph node located in the thoracic cavity. (NCI)
The soft tissue of the thorax.
The vertebrae of the thoracic spine, numbered one through twelve in humans.
Any of the vertebrae situated between the cervical and lumbar vertebrae.
The division of the body lying between the neck and the abdomen. (NCI)
The narrow passage from the mouth to the cavity at the back of the mouth. (NCI)
A primary lymphoid organ generally located in the mediastinum near the thoracic inlet and/or along lateral aspects of the neck.
The narrow, central portion of the thyroid gland that crosses the trachea anteriorly and connects the two lobes of the gland. (NCI)
Endocrine gland(s) adjacent to the trachea in mammals that produce thyroxine and other hormones.
The cone-like lobe of the thyroid gland that is located in the left side of the trachea. (NCI)
The cone-like lobe of the thyroid gland that is located in the right side of the trachea. (NCI)
The triangular prismoid, elongated bony body of the tibia.
The long bone that is medial to the fibula.

CDISC Synonym(s): Tibial Epiphyseal Plate; Tibial Physis; Tibial Plateau Growth Plate
CDISC Definition: A layer of cartilaginous tissue located in the tibia of children and adolescents that separates the epiphysis from the metaphysis and is the site of longitudinal bone growth until skeletal maturity.
A branch of the sciatic nerve that divides into the medial and lateral plantar nerves, and which innervates the muscles of the crus and the skin of the tarsus.
The blood vessels segment that includes the crural artery and the tibial artery.

A muscle that originates from the lateral condyle of tibia, spans the upper two-thirds of the lateral surface of the tibia, and is attached to the first cuneiform and metatarsal bones of the foot. It is a dorsiflexor of the ankle and invertor of the foot.

A muscle in the lower leg, in general extending from the inner posterior borders of the tibia and fibula to the posterior tibial tendon at the posterior aspect of the medial malleolus; primary function is to stabilize the ankle, as well as invert and plantar flex the foot at the ankle.
An arterial trunk that contains parts of the posterior tibial artery and fibular artery.
The joint connecting the lower part of the tibia with the upper part of the tarsus bones, specifically articulating with the talus bone.
One of the terminal digits of the foot. (NCI)
A thin, horny translucent plate covering the end of each toe. (NCI)
The muscular organ in the mouth used in taste perception and food ingestion.
A secondary lymphoid tissue in the mucosa of the pharynx.
The anatomic space in the root of a tooth that contains nerves, blood vessels, and connective tissue. (NCI)
A hard calcified structure in the jaw; primarily used for eating.
The fibrocartilaginous tube extending from the larynx to the bronchi.
An anatomical structure comprised of trachea, bronchi, and bronchioles that terminate with the alveolar ducts, sacs, and alveoli. (NCI)
A combination of syndesmosis and synovial joints formed by the articulation of the talus with the navicular and the calcaneus with the cuboid.
A carpal bone on the thumb side of the hand that articulates with the 1st and 2nd metacarpals. (NCI)
A condyloid synovial joint within the wrist articulating the trapezium bone to the trapezoid bone.

One of a pair of flat, large, triangular muscles that extend from the external occipital protuberance and the medial third of the superior nuchal line of the occipital bone to the middle of the back. The trapezius muscle is involved in moving the shoulder and arm. (NCI)
A carpal bone located between the trapezium and capitate bones. (NCI)
A condyloid synovial joint within the wrist articulating the trapezoid bone to the capitate bone.
A carpal bone located between the lunate and pisiform bones. (NCI)
The point of articulation in the wrist between the hamate and the triquetral bones.
The point of articulation in the wrist between the lunate and the triquetral bones.
A muscle of the proximal arm/forelimb, in general extending from the scapula and humerus to the olecranon of the ulna; primary function is extension of humeroulnar joint.
A fibrous membrane that attaches to, and provides support for, the tricuspid valve leaflets.
A cardiac valve located between the right atrium and ventricle.
The cusp of the tricuspid valve that is located between the atrioventricular orifice and the conus arteriosus.
NCI Preferred Term: Anterior Cusp of the Tricuspid Valve

CDISC Definition: The portion of the tricuspid valve annulus that attaches to both the posterior and lateral tricuspid valve leaflets.
NCI Preferred Term: Posterior Annulus of the Tricuspid Valve

CDISC Definition: The cusp of the tricuspid valve that is located posterior and on the margin of the right ventricle.
NCI Preferred Term: Posterior Cusp of the Tricuspid Valve

CDISC Definition: The cusp of the tricuspid valve that is attached to the right and left fibrous trigones and the atrial and ventricular septa.
NCI Preferred Term: Septal Cusp of the Tricuspid Valve

CDISC Definition: A cranial nerve extending from the pons, which innervates the skin, mucous membranes, and masticatory muscles of the head.
A bony protrusion on the femoral bone to which muscles are attached. (NCI)
A synovial bursa on the outer side of the hip that is located between the greater trochanter bone, the tendon of the gluteus medius, and the iliotibial tract.
The cranial nerve that controls the superior oblique muscle of the eye. (NCI)
The body excluding the head, neck and appendages.

The inner most layer of the blood vessel wall. The consistency of the intima will vary depending on the type of blood vessel, but will always have an endothelial layer with a basal lamina. It may contain collagen and elastic fibers. (NCI)
A thin membrane that separates the external auditory canal from the middle ear.
The prismatic, elongated bony body of the ulna.
The bone that contains the olecranon process, lies between the radiohumeral joint and the carpus, and is adjacent to the radius.
An artery of the forearm; in general it arises from the brachial artery just below the elbow and forms numerous branches supplying the forearm, wrist and hand.
A nerve arising from spinal nerves C8, T1 and T2, which innervates the flexor muscles of the arm/forelimb and skin of the arm/forelimb and lateral manus.
Either of two arteries located in the umbilical cord.
Extraembryonic structure that connects the fetus to the placenta.
The vein located in the umbilical cord.
The depression or scar on the abdomen that marks the former site of attachment of the umbilical cord. (NCI)
A portion of the pancreas that extends behind the superior mesenteric artery and superior mesenteric vein. (NCI)
A lymph node located in the upper region of the neck. (NCI)
The soft tissue of the upper limb(s).
The sinuses and those parts of the respiratory system above the trachea. It includes the nares, nasopharynx, oropharynx, larynx, vocal cords, glottis and upper trachea.
The division of the urinary tract comprising the kidney and the ureters.
A cord of fibrous tissue that extends from the urinary bladder to the umbilicus; the urachus is a remnant of the fetal urinary canal.
The tube that extends from each kidney to the urinary bladder.
The opening of the ureter in the bladder that is situated at the lateral angle of the trigone.
The tube that extends from the urinary bladder to the urethral opening.
The portion of the urethra that extends from the meatus to the membranous urethra. (NCI)
The portion of the urethra that spans the corpus spongiosum. (NCI)
The portion of the urethra that is located on the posterior aspect of the urogenital diaphragm. (NCI)
That part of the male urethra that passes through the prostate gland. (NCI)
One or both of the muscles that surround the urethra and contract to control the flow of urine, either involuntarily (the internal sphincter) or voluntarily (the external sphincter).
The organs involved in the creation and excretion of urine. (NCI)

An artery that arises most often as a branch of the anterior division of the internal iliac artery; it continues medially in the pelvis within the base of the broad ligament, to the exterior surface of the uterus where it branches into the descending, transverse, and ascending divisions, which further branch into the following: the helicine branches that supply the uterus; the vaginal branch, which anastomoses with the vaginal artery to supply the vagina; the ovarian branch, which anastomoses with ovarian artery to supply the ovaries; and the tubal branch that supplies the fallopian tubes.
The portion of the uterus that connects the oviduct to the corpus uteri.
Any of the ligaments attached to the uterus, which may include the anterior, posterior, lateral, sacro-uterine, and round ligaments.
The tissue that forms the wall of the uterus.
A hollow muscular organ within which the fertilized egg implants and the embryo/fetus develops during pregnancy.
The pigmented layer of the eyeball between the tough, white outer coat of the eye and the retina. (NCI)
The female genital canal, extending from the uterus to the vulva. (NCI)
The external opening of the vagina, which is located within the vulva below the urethral opening.
The tissue layers that enclose the vaginal canal. (NCI)

A cranial nerve arising from the medulla oblongata, which provides efferent parasympathetic innervation to tissues and viscera in the neck, thorax and abdomen; it also includes somatic and visceral afferent nerve fibers.
A duct carrying spermatozoa from the epididymides to the urethra.
A muscle in the quadriceps femoris muscle group between the vastus lateralis and vastus medialis deep to the rectus femoris; primary function is the extension of the femorotibial joint.
A muscle in the quadriceps femoris muscle group lateral to the vastus intermedius; primary function is the extension of the femorotibial joint.
A muscle in the quadriceps femoris muscle group medial to the vastus intermedius; primary function is the extension of the femorotibial joint.
A blood vessel that carries blood towards the heart.
The two major veins (caudal or cranial) that carry deoxygenated blood from the body and drain into the right atrium of the heart.
An endothelium-lined passageway or channel that drains venous blood.
Any of the small bones that comprise the vertebral column.
The first branch of the subclavian artery that ascends both sides of the neck and merges at the middle line to form the basilar artery at the level of the pons.
The series of vertebrae and other tissues extending from the skull to the last tailbone.
The area where the ureter joins to the urinary bladder.
A cranial nerve extending from the inner ear and entering the cranial cavity through the internal auditory foramen where it joins the brainstem.

A pair of small bands of muscle that stretch from the thyroid cartilage in front to the arytenoid cartilage in back of the larynx. The vocal cords help prevent food entering the lungs and produce sound through vibration. (NCI)
A thin, paired or unpaired, trapezoidal bone of the skull located in the floor of the nasal cavity. The vomer forms the posterior and inferior parts of the nasal septum. (NCI)
The area of the vulva surrounding the vaginal orifice and enclosed by the labia minora.
The external, visible part of the female genitalia surrounding the urethral and vaginal opening(s).
The body region comprising the vulva and vagina.
The abdominal circumference at the navel. (NCI)
The ring of lymphoid tissue located in the pharynx, consisting of the pharyngeal, tubal, palatine, and lingual tonsils. (NCI)
An area of low density in the femoral neck, as seen by radiography, which is bounded by the principle compressive, secondary compressive and primary tensile trabeculae.
Stiff sensory hairs that project outward from the snout.

A group of muscles in the upper extremity, the extensor carpi radialis longus, extensor carpi radialis brevis, extensor digitorum, extensor digiti minimi, extensor carpi ulnaris, extensor indicis, extensor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis brevis, and abductor pollicis longus muscles; primary function is extension and abduction of the wrist and extension of the fingers.
The tendons located along the back part of the forearm that cross to the thumb side of the wrist and connect muscles of the forearm to the base of hand bones, enabling extension of the wrist. (NCI)

A group of muscles in the upper extremity, the flexor carpi radialis, palmaris longus, flexor carpi ulnaris, flexor digitorum superficialis, flexor digitorum profundus, and flexor pollicis longus muscles; primary function is flexion, adduction, and abduction of the wrist, and flexion and adduction of the fingers.
The tendons located along the inside of the forearm that cross at the wrist and connect muscles of the forearm to wrist and hand bones, enabling flexion of the wrist. (NCI)
A joint between the distal end of the radius and the proximal row of carpal bones. (NCI)
The cartilage just below the sternal body. (NCI)
A bone of the eye socket that articulates with the maxilla, the temporal bone, the sphenoid bone and the frontal bone, to form the prominence of the cheek.
Terminology relevant to the reason for why an arm and/or an actual arm is null.
NCI Preferred Term: CDISC SDTM Arm Null Reason Response Terminology

CDISC Definition: The subject, who met eligibility criteria, was assigned to an arm but was not treated. (NCI)
NCI Preferred Term: Subject Assigned to Arm But Not Treated

CDISC Definition: The subject, who met eligibility criteria, was not assigned to an arm and was not treated. (NCI)
The potential subject who does not meet eligibility (inclusion/exclusion) criteria during the screening period.
An indication that the subject did not complete the screening process.
The subject, who met eligibility criteria, was assigned to an arm but received treatment not associated with any of the planned arms.

CDISC Definition: Membrane proteins in the acetylcholine receptor family that bind to and mediate the neurotransmission of acetylcholine. They can be considered as autoantigens and are commonly associated with the autoimmune disease myasthenia gravis.

CDISC Synonym(s): A Disintegrin and Metalloproteinase with Thrombospondin Type 1 Motif 13; ADAM Metallopeptidase With Thrombospondin Type 1 Motif 13; Von Willebrand Coagulation Factor Cleaving Protease
CDISC Definition: An antigen encoded by the ADAMTS13 gene and cleaves von Willebrand Factor (vWF). It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune disease immune-mediated thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (iTTP).
NCI Preferred Term: A Disintegrin and Metalloproteinase with Thrombospondin Motifs 13

CDISC Synonym(s): Adenylate Kinase 6; AK5; AK6; ATP-AMP Transphosphorylase 5
CDISC Definition: An antigen encoded by the AK5 gene and is involved in regulating the adenine nucleotide composition. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune limbic encephalitis.

A group of autoimmune substances found in the adrenal gland that may be comprised of (but not limited to) 21-hydroxylase, 17-hydroxylase and P450scc (cholesterol side-chain cleavage enzyme). They are commonly associated with autoimmune adrenal diseases, such as adrenocortical insufficiency and Addison's disease.

CDISC Synonym(s): Almond Allergen; Prunus amygdalus Antigen; Prunus dulcis Antigen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) from the seed of the species Prunus dulcis (almond) that are considered as food allergen(s).
The approximately 14 kDa milk whey protein and a component of lactose synthase that is considered as a food allergen.

CDISC Synonym(s): American Cockroach Allergen; Periplaneta americana Antigen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) from the species Periplaneta americana (American cockroach) that are considered as insect allergen(s).

CDISC Synonym(s): American House Dust Mite Allergen; Dermatophagoides farinae Antigen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) from the species Dermatophagoides farinae (American house dust mite) that are considered as insect allergen(s).

One or more of the antigen(s) from the aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase family and are enzymes that attach the appropriate amino acids onto their corresponding tRNAs. This family of proteins may be comprised of (but not limited to) histidyl- (Jo-1), threonyl- (PL-7), alanyl- (PL-12), glycyl- (EJ), isoleucyl- (OJ), asparaginyl- (KS), phenylalanyl- (Zo), and tyrosyl- (YRS) tRNA synthetases. They can be considered as autoantigens and are commonly associated with the autoimmune diseases polymyositis and dermatomyositis.

CDISC Synonym(s): Alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazole propionate Receptor 1; AMPA-Selective Glutamate Receptor 1; GluA1; GluR1; Glutamate Ionotropic Receptor AMPA Type Subunit 1; Glutamate Receptor 1
CDISC Definition: An antigen encoded by the GRIA1 gene that binds to and mediates the neurotransmission of glutamate. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune encephalopathies.

CDISC Synonym(s): Alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazole propionate Receptor 2; AMPA-Selective Glutamate Receptor 2; GluA2; Glutamate Ionotropic Receptor AMPA Type Subunit 2; Glutamate receptor 2, GluR2
CDISC Definition: An antigen encoded by the GRIA2 gene that binds to and mediates the neurotransmission of glutamate. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune encephalopathies.

The ligand-gated, transmembrane proteins in the glutamate receptor family that bind to and mediate the neurotransmission of glutamate. They can be considered as autoantigens and are commonly associated with autoimmune encephalopathies.

An antigen encoded by the AMPH gene that is involved in both exocytosis and cytoskeletal arrangement. It can be considered as a neuronal autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune neurodegenerative disorders related to cancer, such as paraneoplastic neurologic syndrome.
Antigen(s) from a mix of animals that are considered as animal allergen(s).

CDISC Synonym(s): AQP-4; Aquaporin 4 Receptor; Aquaporin 4 Water Channel; Mercurial-Insensitive Water Channel
CDISC Definition: An antigen encoded by the AQP4 gene that forms water-selective channels in the plasma membranes of cells, and thereby regulates brain water homeostasis. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune disease neuromyelitis optica.

CDISC Synonym(s): Anthrax Toxin Protective Antigen; Bacillus anthracis PA
CDISC Definition: The 83 kDa cell-binding protein from Bacillus anthracis that forms membrane spanning pores which mediate and allow the translocation of the anthrax toxin proteins into the cytoplasm of the host cells.

An antigen encoded by the BPI gene and an endogenous antibiotic, cytotoxic protein in the innate immune system. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune diseases inflammatory bowel disease, systemic lupus erythematosus and rheumatoid arthritis.

CDISC Synonym(s): Musa Species Antigen; Musa spp Antigen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) from the fruit of the various species under the genus Musa that are considered as food allergen(s). This includes both edible (dessert) banana and cooking banana (plantains).

A group of autoimmune substances found in the extracellular matrix basement membrane that may be comprised of (but not limited to) collagens and basement membrane proteins. They are commonly associated with the autoimmune diseases bullous pemphigoid, glomerulonephritis, Goodpasture's disease, and rheumatoid arthritis.

CDISC Synonym(s): BMZ BP180; BP180; BPAG2; Bullous Pemphigoid Antigen 2; Collagen Type XVII Alpha 1 Chain
CDISC Definition: An antigen encoded by the COL17A1 gene and is involved in the attachment of keratinocytes to the basement membrane. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune disease bullous pemphigoid.

CDISC Synonym(s): BMZ BP230; BP230; BPAG1; Bullous Pemphigoid Antigen 1; Dystonin
CDISC Definition: An antigen encoded by the DST gene and promotes cytoskeleton networking. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune disease bullous pemphigoid.
Antigen(s) in the Hymenoptera venom from a mix of bees that are considered as insect allergen(s).
NCI Preferred Term: Multiple Bee Mix Hymenoptera venom Antigens

CDISC Synonym(s): Beef Allergen; Bos taurus Meat Antigen; Cow Meat Antigen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) in the meat of the species Bos taurus (cow) that are considered as food allergen(s).

CDISC Synonym(s): Bermuda Grass Pollen Allergen; Cynodon dactylon Pollen Antigen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) in the pollen of the species Cynodon dactylon (Bermuda grass) that are considered as plant allergen(s).
The approximately 18.4 kDa lipocalin, a major milk whey protein that is considered as a food allergen.

CDISC Synonym(s): Apo-H; Apolipoprotein H; B2GPI; Beta-2-Glycoprotein I
CDISC Definition: An antigen of the cardiolipin-binding protein encoded by the APOH gene. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune diseases antiphospholipid syndrome and systemic rheumatic diseases like systemic lupus erythematosus.
Antigen(s) from cow milk that has been boiled, that are considered as food allergen(s).
The approximately 220-250 kDa cell surface, adhesin protein and the virulence factor for Bordetella pertussis.
A mixture of fimbriae antigens from Bordetella pertussis.
The approximately 69 kDa cell surface, autotransporter protein and the virulence factor for Bordetella pertussis.
The approximately 105 kDa secreted exotoxin and the virulence factor for Bordetella pertussis.
The approximately 18 kDa protein encoded by the bacteria Borrelia burgdorferi which is a Lyme disease antigen.

CDISC Synonym(s): Borrelia burgdorferi OspC; Borrelia burgdorferi Outer surface protein C; Borrelia burgdorferi Protein p23
CDISC Definition: The approximately 23 kDa protein encoded by the bacteria Borrelia burgdorferi which is a Lyme disease antigen.
The approximately 28 kDa protein encoded by the bacteria Borrelia burgdorferi which is a Lyme disease antigen.
The approximately 30 kDa protein encoded by the bacteria Borrelia burgdorferi which is a Lyme disease antigen.
The approximately 39 kDa protein encoded by the bacteria Borrelia burgdorferi which is a Lyme disease antigen.
The approximately 41 kDa protein encoded by the bacteria Borrelia burgdorferi which is a Lyme disease antigen.
The approximately 45 kDa protein encoded by the bacteria Borrelia burgdorferi which is a Lyme disease antigen.
The approximately 58 kDa protein encoded by the bacteria Borrelia burgdorferi which is a Lyme disease antigen.
The approximately 66 kDa protein encoded by the bacteria Borrelia burgdorferi which is a Lyme disease antigen.
The approximately 93 kDa protein encoded by the bacteria Borrelia burgdorferi which is a Lyme disease antigen.

CDISC Synonym(s): Acer negundo Pollen Antigen; Box Elder Pollen Allergen; Boxelder Pollen Antigen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) in the pollen of the species Acer negundo (box elder tree) that are considered as plant allergen(s).

CDISC Synonym(s): Budgerigar Dropping Allergen; Melopsittacus undulatus Dropping Antigen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) in the feces of the species Melopsittacus undulatus (budgerigar) that are considered as animal allergen(s).

CDISC Synonym(s): Budgerigar Feather Allergen; Melopsittacus undulatus Feather Antigen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) in the feather of the species Melopsittacus undulatus (budgerigar) that are considered as animal allergen(s).

CDISC Synonym(s): Budgerigar Serum Antigens; Budgerigar Serum Protein Allergen; Melopsittacus undulatus Serum Proteins
CDISC Definition: Protein(s) in the serum of the species Melopsittacus undulatus (budgerigar) that are considered as animal allergen(s).

CDISC Synonym(s): Brown Crab Antigen; Cancer pagurus Allergen; Rock Crab Antigen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) from the species Cancer pagurus (brown crab) that are considered as food allergen(s).

CDISC Synonym(s): CA8; Carbonic anhydrase VIII; Carbonic anhydrase-related protein; CARP
CDISC Definition: An antigen encoded by the CA8 gene and regulates calcium release and neuron mobility. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration and autoimmune dementia.

An antigen of the diphosphatidylglycerol lipid found uniquely in the inner membrane of mitochondria. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune diseases antiphospholipid syndrome and systemic rheumatic diseases.
The approximately 20-25 kDa milk protein that is the dominant constituent of total milk protein and is considered as a food allergen.

CDISC Synonym(s): Anacardium occidentale Nut Antigen; Cashew Nut Allergen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) from the seed of the species Anacardium occidentale (cashew nut) that are considered as food allergen(s).

CDISC Synonym(s): Cat Dander Allergen; Domestic Cat Dander Antigen; Felis catus Dander Antigen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) in the dander (skin flakes) of the species Felis catus (domestic cat) that are considered as animal allergen(s).

Antigen(s) of the lysosomal proteinase or endopeptidase family and are encoded by the CTS gene. They can be considered as autoantigens and are commonly associated with systemic vasculitis, inflammatory rheumatic diseases, autoimmune hepatitis, and chronic inflammatory bowel diseases.

CDISC Synonym(s): CENP-A; Centromere Autoantigen A; Centromere Protein A
CDISC Definition: An antigen of the centromere protein encoded by the CENPA gene, with a designation of A. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune disease CREST syndrome.

CDISC Synonym(s): CENP-B; Centromere Protein B; Major Centromere Autoantigen B
CDISC Definition: An antigen of the centromere protein encoded by the CENPB gene, with a designation of B. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune disease CREST syndrome.

Antigen(s) of the centromere protein family and are encoded by the CENP gene. They can be considered as autoantigens and are commonly associated with the autoimmune diseases Sjogren's syndrome, systemic sclerosis, and CREST syndrome.
Antigen(s) from a mix of workplace or household chemicals that are considered as allergen(s).

CDISC Synonym(s): Chicken Meat Allergen; Gallus domesticus Meat Antigen; Gallus gallus Meat Antigen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) in the meat of the species Gallus domesticus (chicken) that are considered as food allergen(s).
The mixture of DNA and proteins that form the chromosomes. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune disease systemic lupus erythematosus.
The approximately 150 kDa secreted protein toxin and the virulence factor for Clostridium tetani.
The purified and detoxified form of the Clostridium tetani toxin. Toxicity of this toxin is suppressed or inactivated either by heat or with formaldehyde.
An antigen encoded by the F9 gene and plays a role in the intrinsic pathway of blood coagulation through the mediation of proteolysis that converts factor X into an active protease.
An antigen encoded by the F8 gene and plays a role in the modulation of coagulation factor VIII activity and blood coagulation.

A member of the collagen superfamily with a Roman numeral designation of VII. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune diseases bullous pemphigoid and epidermolysis bullosa acquisita.

CDISC Synonym(s): Common Buckwheat Allergen; Fagopyrum esculentum Antigen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) from the seed of the species Fagopyrum esculentum (common buckwheat) that are considered as food allergen(s).

CDISC Synonym(s): Ambrosia artemisiifolia Pollen Antigen; Ambrosia elatior Pollen Antigen; Common Ragweed Pollen Allergen; Short Ragweed Pollen Antigen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) in the pollen of the species Ambrosia artemisiifolia (common ragweed) that are considered as plant allergen(s).

An antigen of the "q" subcomponent of the C1 complement protein complex. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune diseases systemic lupus erythematosus and severe rheumatoid arthritis.
An antigen of the cleaved "d" fragment of the C3 complement protein. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune disease systemic lupus erythematosus.

CDISC Synonym(s): MAC; Membrane Attack Complex; TCC; Terminal Complement Complex
CDISC Definition: A protein complex composed of five activated complement proteins (C5b, C6, C7, C8 and C9) and a cytolytic effector of innate and adaptive immunity, which may be the target of autoantibodies. MAC forms pores in the plasma membrane of pathogens or targeted cells, leading to osmolysis and cell death.

CDISC Synonym(s): Glycoprotein GP135; Neural Cell Surface Protein F3
CDISC Definition: An antigen encoded by the CNTN1 gene that functions as a cell adhesion molecule, and plays a role in the formation of axon connections in the developing nervous system. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune neuropathies.

An antigen encoded by the CNTNAP1 gene and is involved in the organization of myelinated axons and neuronal signaling. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune neuropathies.

An antigen encoded by the CNTNAP2 gene and is involved in the structural organization of axons. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune encephalitis and Morvan syndrome.

CDISC Synonym(s): Corn Allergen; Maize Antigen; Zea mays Antigen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) from the fruit (i.e. kernel/maize) of the species Zea mays (corn) that are considered as food allergen(s).

CDISC Synonym(s): Common Hazel Nut Antigen; Common Hazelnut Antigen; Corylus avellana Nut Allergen; European Hazel Nut Antigen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) from the fruit of the species Corylus avellana (common hazel) that are considered as food allergen(s).
The purified and detoxified form of the Corynebacterium diphtheriae toxin. Toxicity of this toxin is suppressed or inactivated either by heat or with formaldehyde.

CDISC Synonym(s): Bos taurus Dander Antigen; Cattle Dander Antigen; Cow Dander Allergen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) in the dander (skin flakes) of the species Bos taurus (cow) that are considered as animal allergen(s).
Antigen(s) from the milk produced by a cow that are considered as food allergen(s).
Antigen(s) from cow milk that has been curdled and strained, that are considered as food allergen(s).

CDISC Synonym(s): Avena sativa Cultivated Pollen Antigen; Avena sativa Pollen Antigen; Cultivated Oat Pollen Allergen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) in the pollen of the species Avena sativa (cultivated oat) that are considered as plant allergen(s).

CDISC Synonym(s): Collapsin Response Mediator Protein 5; CRMP5; CV2
CDISC Definition: An antigen encoded by the DPYSL5 gene that regulates neurite outgrowth and neurogenesis. It can be considered as a neuronal autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune neurodegenerative disorders related to cancer, such as paraneoplastic neurologic syndrome.
An antigen of the citrulline-containing peptide with a cyclic structure. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune disease rheumatoid arthritis.

An antigen encoded by the NT5C1A gene and is involved in the dephosphorylation of nucleotides to nucleosides. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune disease sporadic inclusion body myositis.
An antigen encoded by the PHGDH gene and is involved in the serine biosynthesis pathway. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune liver diseases.
Antigen(s) in the mix of foods made from mammalian milk that are considered as food allergen(s).

CDISC Synonym(s): DNase B; Group A Streptococcus Deoxyribonuclease-B
CDISC Definition: The B subtype of nuclease produced by group A beta-hemolytic streptococci.

An antigen of the cell-cell adhesion protein encoded by the DSG1 gene. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune diseases pemphigus foliaceus and pemphigus vulgaris.
An antigen of the cell-cell adhesion protein encoded by the DSG3 gene. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune disease pemphigus vulgaris.

An antigen encoded by the DPP6 gene that binds to and regulates the biophysical characteristics of voltage-gated potassium channels. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune encephalitis.
NCI Preferred Term: A-Type Potassium Channel Modulatory Protein DPP6

CDISC Synonym(s): Canis familiaris Dander Antigen; Canis lupus familiaris Dander Antigen; Dog Dander Allergen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) in the dander (skin flakes) of the species Canis lupus familiaris (dog) that are considered as animal allergen(s).

An antigen encoded by the DRD2 gene and is involved in dopamine binding, angiogenesis inhibition, and receptor signaling. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune encephalitic syndromes and neuropsychiatric abnormalities.

CDISC Synonym(s): Deoxyribonucleic Acid; Double-stranded DNA; ds-DNA; dsDNA
CDISC Definition: A long linear double-stranded polymer formed from nucleotides attached to a deoxyribose backbone; associated with the transmission of genetic information.
Antigen(s) from the clear and liquid substance around the yolk of an egg that are considered as food allergen(s).

An antigen encoded by the GARS1 gene that regulates glycyl-transfer RNA synthesis (attaches glycine to tRNA). It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune diseases anti-synthetase syndrome, polymyositis and dermatomyositis.
A group of autoimmune substances found in the endometrium. They are commonly associated with autoimmune endometriosis.
Antigen(s) in the endomysium that can be considered as autoantigens and are commonly associated with the autoimmune diseases dermatitis herpetiformis and celiac disease.

CDISC Synonym(s): English Plantain Pollen Allergen; Plantago lanceolata Pollen Antigen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) in the pollen of the species Plantago lanceolata (English plantain) that are considered as plant allergen(s).

CDISC Synonym(s): English Walnut Allergen; Juglans regia Antigen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) from the fruit(s) of the species Juglans regia (English walnut) that are considered as food allergen(s).
The approximately 110 kDa structural protein that forms the nucleocapsid of the Epstein-Barr virus.

A complex of viral antigens from the Epstein-Barr virus expressed during the lytic cycle. It is comprised of restricted (EA-R) components, found only in the cytoplasm, and diffuse (EA-D) components, located in the nucleus and the cytoplasm.

CDISC Synonym(s): EBV EA-D; Epstein-Barr Virus Early Antigen Diffuse Component; Epstein-Barr Virus Early Antigen-Diffuse
CDISC Definition: The approximately 46-55 kDa lytic protein from the Epstein-Barr virus and is the diffuse component of the Epstein-Barr virus-induced early antigen (EA) complex.
NCI Preferred Term: Epstein-Barr Virus Early Antigen Diffuse Component

CDISC Definition: The approximately 66 kDa DNA-binding protein with a designation nuclear antigen 1, from the 6 nuclear antigens produced by the Epstein-Barr virus.
One or more proteins from the 6 nuclear antigens (EBNA 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and/or 6) produced by the Epstein-Barr virus.

CDISC Synonym(s): Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus Antigen; European House Dust Mite Allergen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) from the species Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus (European house dust mite) that are considered as insect allergen(s).

CDISC Synonym(s): ENAs; Extractable Nuclear Antigens; Saline-extracted Nuclear Antigens
CDISC Definition: A group of autoimmune substances found in the nucleus of a cell which can be extracted from the saline soluble fraction of cells, and may be comprised of (but not limited to) ribonucleoproteins, Smith antigens, Sjogren's antigens, Scl-70 and/or Jo-1 antigens.
A fibrillar actin polymer. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune hepatitis and primary biliary cirrhosis.

CDISC Synonym(s): Atlantic Cod Antigen; Cod Antigen; Gadus morhua Allergen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) from the species Gadus morhua (Atlantic cod) that are considered as food allergen(s).

The type B receptor in the GABA receptor family that binds to and mediates the neurotransmission of gamma-aminobutyric acid. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune disease limbic encephalitis.

A sialic acid-containing glycosphingolipid antigen and a component of the cell plasma membrane that modulates cell signal transduction, with a designation of GD1a. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune neuropathies such as Guillain-Barre syndrome and multiple sclerosis.

A sialic acid-containing glycosphingolipid antigen and a component of the cell plasma membrane that modulates cell signal transduction, with a designation of GD1b. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune neuropathies such as Guillain-Barre syndrome and multiple sclerosis.

A sialic acid-containing glycosphingolipid antigen and a component of the cell plasma membrane that modulates cell signal transduction, with a designation of GD2. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune neuropathies such as Guillain-Barre syndrome and multiple sclerosis.

A sialic acid-containing glycosphingolipid antigen and a component of the cell plasma membrane that modulates cell signal transduction, with a designation of GD3. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune neuropathies such as Guillain-Barre syndrome and multiple sclerosis.

A sialic acid-containing glycosphingolipid antigen and a component of the cell plasma membrane that modulates cell signal transduction, with a designation of GM1. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune neuropathies such as Guillain-Barre syndrome and multiple sclerosis.

It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune neuropathies such as Guillain-Barre syndrome and multiple sclerosis.

It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune neuropathies such as Guillain-Barre syndrome and multiple sclerosis.

A sialic acid-containing glycosphingolipid antigen and a component of the cell plasma membrane that modulates cell signal transduction, with a designation of GM4. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune neuropathies such as Guillain-Barre syndrome and multiple sclerosis.

A sialic acid-containing glycosphingolipid antigen and a component of the cell plasma membrane that modulates cell signal transduction, with a designation of GQ1b. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune neuropathies such as Guillain-Barre syndrome and multiple sclerosis.

A sialic acid-containing glycosphingolipid antigen and a component of the cell plasma membrane that modulates cell signal transduction, with a designation of GT1a. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune neuropathies such as Guillain-Barre syndrome and multiple sclerosis.

A sialic acid-containing glycosphingolipid antigen and a component of the cell plasma membrane that modulates cell signal transduction, with a designation of GT1b. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune neuropathies such as Guillain-Barre syndrome and multiple sclerosis.

CDISC Synonym(s): Blattella germanica Antigen; German Cockroach Allergen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) from the species Blattella germanica (German cockroach) that are considered as insect allergen(s).
An antigen and alcohol-soluble fraction of gluten from wheat and other grains that is considered as a food allergen.
One or more of the gliadin peptides that have been deamidated (where glutamine residues are turned into glutamic acid). Gliadin is a component of gluten which is considered as a food allergen.

CDISC Submission Value: GLIAL FIBRILLARY ACIDIC PROTEIN ALPHA SUBUNIT
CDISC Definition: The alpha isoform (i.e. the canonical form) of the glial fibrillary acidic protein which is involved in both neuronal maintenance and astrocyte morphology and motility. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune astrocytopathy.

CDISC Synonym(s): Glial Nuclear Type 1 Autoantigen; Sox1; Sox1 Nuclear Antigen; Transcription Factor SOX-1
CDISC Definition: An antigen encoded by the Sox1 gene. This protein is a transcription activator and may be involved in neuronal development. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune neuropathies.

A group of autoimmune substances found in the glomerular basement membrane that may be comprised of (but not limited to) the alpha 3 chain of type IV collagen. They are commonly associated with autoimmune disease Goodpasture syndrome.

CDISC Synonym(s): GAD67; Glutamate decarboxylase 67; Glutamic Acid Decarboxylase 67
CDISC Definition: An antigen of the 67 kDa isoform of GAD which is encoded by the GAD1 gene. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune disease type 1 diabetes.

CDISC Synonym(s): GLRA1; Glycine Glycine Receptor 48 kDa Subunit; GlyRa1

The approximately 70-94 kDa secreted, immunogenic glycoprotein, with potential catalase activity, encoded by the M antigen gene, from the fungus Histoplasma capsulatum.

The approximately 40 kDa envelope glycoprotein encoded from the human immunodeficiency virus 1.

CDISC Definition: The approximately 55 kDa Gag polyprotein product encoded by the human immunodeficiency virus 1. It is a precursor protein for several proteins that form the core structure of the HIV-1 virus.
The approximately 65 kDa protein subunit of the reverse transcriptase encoded by the human immunodeficiency virus 1.
The approximately 140 kDa envelope glycoprotein from the human immunodeficiency virus 2.
The approximately 36 kDa transmembrane, envelope glycoprotein from the human immunodeficiency virus 2.

A group of human leukocyte antigens that are typically expressed as transmembrane glycoproteins on the surface of all nucleated cells, and consist mainly of (but are not limited to) HLA-A, HLA-B and HLA-C.
A group of human leukocyte antigens that are typically expressed on professional antigen-presenting cells, and consist mainly of (but are not limited to) HLA-DR, HLA-DP and HLA-DQ.

Antigen(s) from house dust that are considered as allergen(s).

CDISC Definition: An antigen encoded by the INSM2 gene and regulates insulin secretion. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune disease type 1 diabetes.

CDISC Definition: A glycoprotein encoded by the CBLIF gene, produced by the parietal cells in the stomach, and is necessary for the absorption of vitamin B12 (cobalamin) in the distal ileum of the small intestine. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune disease pernicious anemia.

CDISC Synonym(s): IA-2; ICA512; Islet Antigen 2; Islet Cell Autoantigen 3; PTP-IA2; Receptor-type Tyrosine-protein Phosphatase-like N
CDISC Definition: An antigen encoded by the PTPRN gene and regulates insulin secretion. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune disease type 1 diabetes.
A group of autoimmune substances found in the pancreatic islet beta cells. They are commonly associated with the autoimmune disease type 1 diabetes.
A group of autoimmune substances found in the cytoplasm of pancreatic islet cells that are the target of autoantibodies. They are commonly associated with the autoimmune disease type 1 diabetes.

An antigen encoded by the INGAP gene and can stimulate the creation of new islet mass from adult pancreatic progenitor cells. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune diabetes.

CDISC Synonym(s): Cupressus sempervirens Pollen Antigen; Funeral Cypress Pollen Antigen; Italian Cypress Pollen Allergen; Mediterranean Cypress Pollen Antigen

CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) in the pollen of the species Chamaecyparis obtusa (Japanese cypress tree) that are considered as plant allergen(s).

CDISC Synonym(s): Johnson Grass Pollen Allergen; Sorghum halepense Pollen; Sorghum halepense Pollen Antigen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) in the pollen of the species Sorghum halepense (Johnson grass) that are considered as plant allergen(s).

CDISC Synonym(s): June Grass Pollen Antigen; Kentucky Bluegrass Pollen Allergen; Poa pratensis Pollen Antigen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) in the pollen of the species Poa pratensis (Kentucky bluegrass) that are considered as plant allergen(s).
An antigen found in the hemolymph of the species Megathura crenulata (giant keyhole limpet) that is also considered as a food allergen.

A heterodimer (Ku70/Ku80) DNA-binding nuclear protein that is involved in nonhomologous end-joining DNA repair, and the recognition and repair of double-stranded DNA breaks. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune connective tissue diseases and systemic sclerosis.

An antigen encoded by the LTF gene that binds to iron and has antimicrobial function. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune diseases rheumatoid vasculitis and arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, ulcerative colitis, and Crohn's disease.

An antigen encoded by the LGI1 gene and is involved in the regulation of voltage-gated potassium channel assembly and activity. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune encephalitis.
An antigen of the human liver 58 kDa cytosolic polypeptide encoded by the FTCD gene. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with type 2 autoimmune hepatitis.

A group of autoimmune substances in the P450 mixed-function oxidase system that may be comprised of (but not limited to) cytochrome P450 2D6 (LKM type 1), P450 2C9 (LKM type 2) and P450 1A2 (LKM type 3). They are commonly associated with autoimmune hepatitis.

CDISC Synonym(s): CYP2D6; Cytochrome P450 2D6; Liver Kidney Microsomal 1 Antigen
CDISC Definition: An antigen in the cytochrome P450 mixed-function oxidase system and is encoded by the CYP2D6 gene, it is a major drug metabolizing enzyme. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune hepatitis.

CDISC Synonym(s): LDL Receptor Related Protein 4; LRP4; MEGF7; Multiple Epidermal Growth Factor-like Domains 7; Sclerosteosis 2; SOST2
CDISC Definition: An antigen encoded by the LRP4 gene and a regulator of the Wnt signaling that is involved in neuromuscular junction formation. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune disease myasthenia gravis.

An antigen encoded by the PNMA1 gene that may promote apoptosis. It can be considered as a neuronal autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune neurodegenerative disorders related to cancer, such as paraneoplastic neurologic syndrome.

CDISC Synonym(s): Paraneoplastic Antigen Ma2; PNMA2; Ta Antigen
CDISC Definition: An antigen encoded by the PNMA2 gene and regulates apoptosis. It can be considered as a neuronal autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune neurodegenerative disorders related to cancer, such as paraneoplastic neurologic syndrome.

CDISC Synonym(s): CADM-140 Autoantigen; Interferon Induced With Helicase C Domain 1; Melanoma Differentiation-Associated Protein 5
CDISC Definition: An antigen encoded by the IFIH1 gene and is involved in the induction of antiviral responses. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune dermatomyositis and interstitial lung disease.

CDISC Synonym(s): Festuca elatior Pollen Antigen; Lolium arundinaceum Pollen Antigen; Meadow Fescue Pollen Allergen; Tall Fescue Pollen Antigen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) in the pollen of the species Festuca elatior (meadow fescue) that are considered as plant allergen(s).

An antigen encoded by the GRM5 gene and is involved in both glutamate binding and downstream signal transduction. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune encephalitis.

CDISC Synonym(s): Dermatomyositis Autoantigen Mi-2 Alpha; MI-2 Alpha; MI-2a
CDISC Definition: The 220 kDa alpha isoform of the MI-2 antigen encoded by CHD3 gene, which is a helicase in the nucleosome remodeling-deacetylase complex involved in transcription regulation. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the systemic autoimmune myopathy dermatomyositis.

CDISC Synonym(s): Dermatomyositis Autoantigen Mi-2; Major Dermatomyositis-specific Mi-2 Autoantigen
CDISC Definition: Antigens derived from certain helicases in the nucleosome remodeling-deacetylase complex (NuRD) involved in transcription regulation that may be comprised of (but not limited to) two isoforms Mi-2 alpha and Mi-2 beta. They can be considered as autoantigens and are commonly associated with systemic autoimmune myopathy dermatomyositis.

CDISC Synonym(s): Chromodomain-Helicase-DNA-Binding Protein 4; Dermatomyositis Autoantigen Mi-2 Beta; MI-2 Beta; MI-2b
CDISC Definition: The 218 kDa beta isoform of the MI-2 antigen encoded by CHD4 gene, which is a helicase in the nucleosome remodeling-deacetylase complex involved in transcription regulation. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the systemic autoimmune myopathy dermatomyositis.

It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with primary biliary liver cirrhosis and other autoimmune liver diseases.

A group of autoimmune, multienzyme complexes found within the inner and outer lining of the mitochondria that may be comprised of (but not limited to) M1 through M9 antigens. They are commonly associated with autoimmune hepatitis and primary biliary cholangitis/cirrhosis.

CDISC Synonym(s): Mitochondrial Antigen M2; Mitochondrial Autoantigen M2
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) of the inner mitochondrial membrane proteins, with a designation of M2, and may be comprised of (but not limited to) protein X, the E2 component, E1a and E1b subunits of the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex (PDC). They can be considered as autoantigens and are commonly associated with autoimmune hepatitis and primary biliary cholangitis/cirrhosis.
Antigen(s) from a mix of types of sources that are considered as allergen(s).

An antigen encoded by the MORC3 gene that is involved in both RNA binding and nuclear matrix protein binding. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune diseases polymyositis and dermatomyositis.

A group of autoimmune substances found in the myelin sheath, which is a layer of phospholipids and protein found on neuronal axons. They are commonly associated with the autoimmune diseases multiple sclerosis and Guillain-Barre syndrome.

An antigen encoded by the MOG gene and is involved in the myelination of nerves in the central nervous system. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune diseases multiple sclerosis and other demyelinating diseases.

An antigen encoded by the MPO gene that regulates innate immunity through hypohalous acids production. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune systemic vasculitis diseases, cystic fibrosis, COPD and other inflammatory conditions.

A group of autoimmune substances found in the neurons that may be comprised of (but not limited to) Hu, Tr, Yo and Ri proteins. They can be considered as neuronal autoantigens and are commonly associated with autoimmune neurodegenerative disorders related to cancer, such as paraneoplastic neurologic syndrome.

A group of autoimmune substances found in the neurons that may be comprised of (but not limited to) the Hu proteins HuD, HuC, HuR (HuA), and HuB (Hel-N1) and Hel-N2. They can be considered as neuronal autoantigens and are commonly associated with autoimmune neurodegenerative disorders related to cancer, such as paraneoplastic neurologic syndrome.

A group of autoimmune substances found in the neurons that may be comprised of (but not limited to) the Ri proteins Nova-1 and Nova-2. They can be considered as neuronal autoantigens and are commonly associated with autoimmune neurodegenerative disorders related to cancer, such as paraneoplastic neurologic syndrome.

CDISC Synonym(s): ANNA-3 Antigen; DACH1; Dachshund Family Transcription Factor 1; Dachshund-Homolog 1
CDISC Definition: An antigen encoded by the DACH1 gene and regulates gene expression and cell fate determination during development. It can be considered as a neuronal autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune neurodegenerative and paraneoplastic disorders related to cancer.

An antigen of the NMDA receptor that binds to and mediates the neurotransmission of N-methyl-D-aspartic acid and iron. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune encephalitis.

An antigen encoded by the SP100 gene and is involved in promyelocytic leukemia nuclear (PML) body function, transcriptional regulation and DNA binding. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune disease primary biliary cholangitis.
A group of autoimmune substances found in the nucleus of a cell that are the target of autoantibodies.

CDISC Definition: An antigen encoded by the NUP210 gene and is essential for assembly and fusion, spacing and structural integrity of the nuclear pore. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune disease primary biliary cirrhosis.

Antigen(s) from a mix of edible nuts that are considered as food allergen(s).

CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) in the pollen of the species Olea europaea (olive tree) that are considered as plant allergen(s).

CDISC Synonym(s): Northern Red Shrimp Antigen; Northern Shrimp Antigen; Pandalus borealis Allergen
CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) from the species Pandalus borealis (Northern shrimp) that are considered as food allergen(s).

CDISC Synonym(s): Parietaria judaica Pollen Allergen; Parietaria judaica Pollen Antigen; Wall Pellitory (judaica) Pollen Antigen

CDISC Definition: Antigen(s) in the pollen of the species Lolium perenne (perennial ryegrass) that are considered as plant allergen(s).

An antigen of the phospholipid containing serine in the inner cell membrane. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with the autoimmune diseases of antiphospholipid syndrome and systemic sclerosis.

An antigen encoded by the PLA2R1 gene and is involved in the modulation of phospholipase activity. It can be considered as an autoantigen and is commonly associated with autoimmune disease membranous nephropathy.

Antigen(s) of the phosphate-containing lipids. They can be considered as autoantigens and are commonly and mainly associated with the autoimmune diseases antiphospholipid syndrome and systemic rheumatic diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus.

CDISC Definition: The X-ray examination of blood vessels or chambers of the heart after introduction of a radiopaque substance.
Initiation or intensification of orally administered medication(s) that promote diuresis to treat heart failure.
NCI Preferred Term: Oral Diuretic Therapy Augmentation for Heart Failure

CDISC Definition: A postmortem examination of the body.

CDISC Submission Value: CLINICALLY SIGNIFICANT OR RAPID WEIGHT GAIN
CDISC Definition: Weight gain thought to be related to fluid retention.
NCI Preferred Term: Weight Gain Due to Fluid Retention

CDISC Definition: Angiographic evidence of new or worse greater than or equal to 70 percent lesion and/or thrombus in an epicardial coronary artery believed to be responsible for the myocardial ischemic symptoms/signs. (Hicks KA, Tcheng JE, Bozkurt B, Chaitman BR, Cutlip DE, Farb A, Fonarow GC, Jacobs JP, Jaff MR, Lichtman JH, Limacher MC, Mahaffey KW, Mehran, R, Nissen SE, Smith EE, Targum SL. 2014 ACC/AHA Key Data Elements and Definitions For Cardiovascular Endpoint Events In Clinical Trials: a report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Task Force on Clinical Data Standards (Writing Committee to Develop Cardiovascular End Points Data Standards) J Am Coll Cardiol 2014; In Press)

Need for coronary revascularization procedure (PCI or CABG) for the presumed culprit lesion(s). This criterion would be fulfilled if revascularization was undertaken during the unscheduled hospitalization, or subsequent to transfer to another institution without interceding home discharge. (Hicks KA, Tcheng JE, Bozkurt B, Chaitman BR, Cutlip DE, Farb A, Fonarow GC, Jacobs JP, Jaff MR, Lichtman JH, Limacher MC, Mahaffey KW, Mehran, R, Nissen SE, Smith EE, Targum SL. 2014 ACC/AHA Key Data Elements and Definitions For Cardiovascular Endpoint Events In Clinical Trials: a report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Task Force on Clinical Data Standards (Writing Committee to Develop Cardiovascular End Points Data Standards) J Am Coll Cardiol 2014; In Press)
Reduced ability to withstand or participate in activities that induce physical or mental exertion.
Includes dyspnea on exertion, dyspnea at rest, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea.
Unusual tiredness and inability to perform usual activities.

An event where the patient is admitted to the hospital with a primary diagnosis of heart failure (HF), where the length of stay is at least 24 hours (or extends over a calendar date), where the patient exhibits new or worsening symptoms of HF on presentation, has objective evidence of new or worsening HF, and receives initiation or intensification of treatment specifically for HF. (Hicks KA, Tcheng JE, Bozkurt B, Chaitman BR, Cutlip DE, Farb A, Fonarow GC, Jacobs JP, Jaff MR, Lichtman JH, Limacher MC, Mahaffey KW, Mehran, R, Nissen SE, Smith EE, Targum SL. 2014 ACC/AHA Key Data Elements and Definitions For Cardiovascular Endpoint Events In Clinical Trials: a report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Task Force on Clinical Data Standards (Writing Committee to Develop Cardiovascular End Points Data Standards) J Am Coll Cardiol 2014; In Press)
An acute episode of focal or global cerebral or spinal dysfunction caused by intraparenchymal, intraventricular, or subarachnoid hemorrhage.

Biomarker increase (B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP)/ N-terminal pro-BNP (NT-proBNP)) consistent with decompensation of heart failure (such as BNP greater than 500 pg/mL or NT-proBNP greater than 2,000 pg/mL). In patients with chronically elevated natriuretic peptides, a significant increase above baseline is required. (Hicks KA, Tcheng JE, Bozkurt B, Chaitman BR, Cutlip DE, Farb A, Fonarow GC, Jacobs JP, Jaff MR, Lichtman JH, Limacher MC, Mahaffey KW, Mehran, R, Nissen SE, Smith EE, Targum SL. 2014 ACC/AHA Key Data Elements and Definitions For Cardiovascular Endpoint Events In Clinical Trials: a report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Task Force on Clinical Data Standards (Writing Committee to Develop Cardiovascular End Points Data Standards) J Am Coll Cardiol 2014; In Press)
NCI Preferred Term: Increase in B-type Natriuretic Peptide or N-terminal pro-B-type Natriuretic Peptide

CDISC Submission Value: INCREASED JUGULAR VENOUS PRESSURE OR HEPATOJUGULAR REFLUX
CDISC Definition: Increase in the estimated height of the mean jugular venous waveform above the right atrium in cm.
Abnormal collection of fluid in the peritoneal cavity.

Definite evidence of inducible myocardial ischemia believed to be responsible for the myocardial ischemic symptoms/signs, demonstrated by any of the following: a) an early positive exercise stress test, defined as ST elevation of greater than or equal to 2 mm ST depression prior to 5 mets, b) stress echocardiography (reversible wall motion abnormality), c) myocardial scintigraphy (reversible perfusion defect), d) MRI (myocardial perfusion deficit under pharmacologic stress). (Hicks KA, Tcheng JE, Bozkurt B, Chaitman BR, Cutlip DE, Farb A, Fonarow GC, Jacobs JP, Jaff MR, Lichtman JH, Limacher MC, Mahaffey KW, Mehran, R, Nissen SE, Smith EE, Targum SL. 2014 ACC/AHA Key Data Elements and Definitions For Cardiovascular Endpoint Events In Clinical Trials: a report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Task Force on Clinical Data Standards (Writing Committee to Develop Cardiovascular End Points Data Standards) J Am Coll Cardiol 2014; In Press)

CDISC Submission Value: INTRAVENOUS DIURETIC, INOTROPE, OR VASODILATOR THERAPY

In leads V2-V3, the following cut-points apply: greater than or equal to 0.2 mV in men greater than or equal to 40 years, greater than or equal to 0.25 mV in men less than 40 years, and greater than or equal to 0.15 mV in women, or b) ST depression and T-wave changes: new horizontal or down-sloping ST depression greater than or equal to 0.05 mV in two contiguous leads and/or new T inversion greater than or equal to 0.3 mV in two contiguous leads with prominent R wave or R/S ratio greater than 1.
